title: Non-blocking findings from frontend-trade-strategy-tagging's PR review (#406)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #406 (frontend-trade-strategy-tagging), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: frontend/src/pages/PortfolioPage.test.tsx has several pre-existing tests that implicitly rely on async query-start/resolution *timing* rather than deterministic assertions, rather than on the actual DOM each query should produce. Confirmed by direct experiment during this PR's review: reproducing the PR's own earlier (reverted) revision -- adding a second `useClosedTrades()` call at PortfolioPage's own top level to union closed-trades' strategy values into recentStrategies -- causes 'shows a loading state, then the equity stat cards and positions table' to fail with 'Found multiple elements with the text: AAPL' (PositionsTable's AAPL link and TradeJournalPanel's own AAPL link both now resolve by the time the bare `screen.getByText('AAPL')` assertion runs, because starting the closed-trades fetch earlier -- at PortfolioPage's own mount instead of only once TradeJournalPanel mounts deeper in the tree -- gives it enough of a timing head start to resolve before that assertion fires), and 'shows the empty state when the portfolio has no positions' fails because `screen.queryByRole('table')).not.toBeInTheDocument()` implicitly assumes TradeJournalPanel's own closed-trades query (whose default MSW fixture is non-empty) hasn't resolved yet by the time that assertion runs, rather than actually asserting the Trade Journal table can never appear for an empty portfolio. Both are real, pre-existing test-design smells (order/timing-dependent assertions, not fixed by anything in this PR) that constrained a legitimate implementation choice in #406 (unioning closed trades' own strategy values was reverted specifically because of this fragility) -- recommend scoping assertions to the specific table under test (e.g. `within(screen.getByRole('table', { name: 'Positions' })).getByText('AAPL')`) and/or explicitly overriding `GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades` to return an empty list in the empty-portfolio test, rather than relying on implicit query-start ordering either way.

AddPositionDialog's 'recent tags' Autocomplete suggestions (recentStrategies, derived in PortfolioPage from usePortfolio()'s held positions only) don't include a `strategy` value that was only ever used on a trade that's since been closed -- a real, if narrow, behavior gap acknowledged in frontend-trade-strategy-tagging's own `decisions` entry. Worth revisiting once the PortfolioPage test-timing fragility above is fixed (or via an alternative that avoids it, e.g. AddPositionDialog/PortfolioPage pulling GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades lazily only once the dialog is actually opened, rather than PortfolioPage prefetching it unconditionally at mount) -- confirm in practice whether this gap is worth closing at all before doing so.
